paper.title: Improved Regret Analysis for Variance-Adaptive Linear Bandits and Horizon-Free Linear Mixture MDPs

unmapped: Arm set X_k subset of unit l2 ball, may change each round (arbitrary subset, not necessarily convex)
Rewards bounded |r_k| <= 1/2 almost surely; noise is martingale difference with unknown, time-varying conditional variance sigma_k^2 (heteroscedastic), not known to learner
Regret is variance-adaptive in sum_k sigma_k^2
settings.definition_quote: At time step $k$, the learner observes an arm set $\mathcal{X}_k \subseteq \mathbb{B}_2^d(1)$, chooses an arm $x_k \in \mathcal{X}_k$, pulls it. The learner then receives a stochastic reward $r_k = x_k^\T \th^*+\eps_k$ where $\th^* \in \mathbb{B}_2^d(1)$ is an unknown parameter ... we assume that $(i)$ $|r_k|\le [-\fr12,\fr12]$ almost surely, $(ii)$ $\mathbb{E}[\eps_k | \mathcal{F}_k]=0$ ..., and $(iii)$ $\mathbb{E}[\eps_k^2|\mathcal{F}_k]=\sigma_k^2$.

settings.name_in_paper: Linear mixture MDPs with unit cumulative rewards
unmapped: Episodic reinforcement learning (MDP) with K episodes and planning horizon H, not a bandit
Transition kernel is a linear mixture P = sum_i theta*_i P^i of d known base models, theta* in unit l1 ball
Known deterministic reward function r(s,a) in [0,1]
Unit cumulative rewards: sum_h r_h^k in [0,1] for any policy
Horizon-free: regret bound independent of H up to polylog factors
settings.definition_quote: The key modeling assumption of linear mixture MDPs is that the transition probability $P$ is a linear combination of a known set of models $\{P^i\}$, namely, $P=\sum_{i=1}^d \th_i^* P^i$ where $\th^* \in \mathbb{B}_1^d(1)$ is an unknown parameter. ... Unit cumulative rewards:$\sum_{h=1}^H r_h^k \in [0,1]$ for any policy $\pi^k$.

bound.regime: with probability at least 1-2delta, delta <= e^{-1}

symbols.Sigma2: sum_{k=1}^K sigma_k^2, total (unknown) conditional noise variance

source.label: main-thm-bandit
source.quote: VOFUL2 satisfies, with probability at least $1-2\dt$, \mathcal{R}^K =\tilde O\del{d^{1.5} \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^2\ln(1/\dt)} + d^2 \ln(1/\dt)} where $\tilde O$ hides poly-logarithmic dependence on $\{d,K,\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^{2},  \ln(1/\dt)\}$.

results.notes: Paper's K is the horizon (T). Algorithm uses K in L and iota so horizon known. Conclusion states algorithms are not computationally tractable.

source.quote: Note that one can also show that VOFUL2 can be slightly modified to achieve the regret bound of $\tilde O\del[1]{  \min\cbr[1]{d\sqrt{K\ln(1/\dt)}, d^{1.5} \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^K \sig_k^2\ln(1/\dt)}} + d^2 \ln(1/\dt)} $, thus being no worse than OFUL.

results.notes: Not a numbered theorem; sketched in appendix via reduction to OFUL confidence ellipsoid. Exact failure probability not stated precisely.

source.label: main-rl
source.quote: With probability at least 1-$\dt$, \mathcal{R}^K =\sum_{k=1}^K [V^*(s_1^k)-V^k(s_1^k)] = \tilde O(d\sqrt{K\log^2(1/\dt)} + d^2\log (1/\dt))~. where $\tilde O$ hides poly-logarithmic dependence on $\{d,K,H, \ln(1/\dt)\}$.

results.notes: Horizon-free (H only in polylogs). d is number of base models.
